output.evaluation_rationale: PRO-SUP-01 achieved the highest total weighted score because it excelled across all evaluation pillars: it received perfect scores for cost (100) and delivery (100), and very high scores for risk (95), contract (90) and capability (95). When these pillar scores are multiplied by their respective weights and summed, the composite result is 97.5, placing it at rank 1. The other suppliers trade off cost savings against risk and capability. PRO-SUP-02 lowers the cost score to 82.17, which reduces its overall weighted total to 90.26 despite maintaining perfect delivery and strong risk (90) and capability (95) scores. PRO-SUP-03 further reduces the cost score to 69.03 and also has a lower risk score (75), resulting in the lowest total weighted score of 82.66. All three suppliers score 100 on delivery, indicating that delivery performance is not a differentiating factor in this set. The spread shows that a roughly 18‑point drop in cost score (from 100 to 82.17) translates to a 7.2‑point drop in the overall weighted score, while an additional 13‑point drop in risk (from 95 to 75) contributes another 7.8‑point reduction. Thus, while cost savings improve the bottom line, they come at the expense of higher risk exposure and slightly lower overall performance, illustrating the classic cost‑risk trade‑off in supplier selection.

output.commercial_rationale: Titanium Engineering Solutions offers the lowest landed cost ($11,935.63) and the highest total weighted score (97.5). It delivers the required 250 units with a 60‑day buffer before the target date, earning a perfect delivery score. output.risk_acceptance: Acceptable. The supplier’s risk rating is LOW, and audit results are positive. The only residual concern is the synthetic flag on the supplier profile, which warrants external verification of ISO certification and capacity before award.
